target_customer: College students (original social app) and later top college engineers and the recruiters hiring them (TenXList)
problem: Original product helped college students connect socially; the pivot aimed to connect top college engineers with employers through a professional network.
business_model: Unknown; consumer social network then a recruiting network

founders.name: Evan Reas
founders.background_notes: YC page: now founder and CEO of Quanta Ventures. A Wikipedia mirror says Evan Reas launched Likealittle in October 2010; the link between Likealittle and Assembled rests on a retrospective blog read only through a search summary.

founders.name: Shubham Mittal
founders.background_notes: YC page gives the role only.

technical_complexity.rationale: A campus social network and later a directory style professional network are standard web products; no hard technology was cited.

defensibility.rationale: Campus social apps depend on local network effects that were easy to copy and fragile; no other moat was found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source documents an incumbent response; Facebook dominated college social networking at the time.

market_need_then: No dated evidence of demand found for the pivot product; Likealittle was a college flirting network launched in October 2010 per a Wikipedia mirror.

rebrands.why: Pivot to a professional network of top college engineers per the YC directory

brand_strength.rationale: No brand press, community or merch found; a branding search returned nothing relevant.

pivots.from: Assembled (earlier known as Likealittle per a retrospective, unverified)
pivots.to: TenXList, a professional network of top college engineers

outcome_analysis: The cause of Assembled's inactivity is not public. The YC directory shows a pivot to TenXList and an inactive status, and a single retrospective suggests an earlier life as Likealittle with an Andreessen Horowitz round. No post-mortem, shutdown notice or dated press on TenXList was found, so no failure factors are assigned.
notes: Identity caution: the claim that Assembled was Likealittle comes from a Medium retrospective (blocked with HTTP 403 when fetched; seen only in search summary) and was not independently verified. The 1 million dollar a16z round at a stated 10 million dollar valuation comes from a Wikipedia mirror of the Likealittle page and rests on that single source; valuation not recorded because pre or post is not stated; date given as 2011 only because the retrospective says during YC. CB Insights has a Likealittle page that returned HTTP 403. YC directory has no company website. Competitors list is empty: no dated sources found for the pivot product; Mertado and Plurchase surfaced but are unrelated shopping startups.
